additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
examples: Starting to eat a large amount of food again immediately after finishing a meal.
A binge eating episode starting when not hungry at all.
Continuing to eat large amounts despite being full.
Seeking out food even when there are absolutely no physical hunger signals.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

patient_info.stressor_event: Foreclosure on a mortgage or loan
patient_info.stressor: Demetrius and his wife fell behind on payments tied to a small loan they had taken out for his planned boutique café, and the foreclosure process forced him to shelve the dream while taking extra cashier shifts and cutting back on night classes. Across the next 4 months, he began stopping after work for large takeout orders and eating alone in his car or after his wife had gone to sleep, often continuing well past fullness and feeling as if he could not stop once he started. The eating was not driven by physical hunger so much as the privacy and numb routine after dealing with creditors, and his embarrassment grew as receipts and empty containers accumulated where he tried to hide them. He entered psychiatric care after a community clinic social worker helping with foreclosure resources asked about recent coping patterns and arranged an appointment when he described the recurrent loss-of-control eating.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: I’m here because after my cashier shifts I keep buying these huge takeout orders—like enough burgers, fries, chicken, and desserts for a family—and I’ll sit there and eat almost all of it myself before I go home.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I take that first bite, it feels like something in me clicks off, and even while I’m telling myself, 'Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,' my hands just keep reaching for the next thing.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
S052.manifestation: A lot of nights I keep eating until my stomach is tight and hurting so bad I have to lean the seat back in the car or lie still in bed and wait for it to pass.

S053.name: Eating_Without_Hunger
S053.description: Eating large amounts of food when not feeling physically hungry.
S053.manifestation: Most of the time I’m not even hungry when it starts, especially if I already ate dinner with my wife, but I still end up looking for food like I’m trying to shut my head off.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
S054.manifestation: I hide it because I’m ashamed, so I’ll eat in the parking lot or wait until my wife is asleep, then stuff the bags and receipts down in the trash so she won’t see how much I had.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: For the last several months, it’s been happening three or four nights most weeks, and I can’t remember a week since the foreclosure calls started where I didn’t do it at least once.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I still get to my cashier shifts, but I’m spending money we don’t have on food and keeping more secrets from my wife, which makes home feel tense and dishonest.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about 4 months, since the foreclosure process really started and I had to give up the café plan.
